releases.body:
Patch release. **`npx oc2-memory install` works now** — it silently did nothing in 0.1.0.

## Fixed

The installer CLI's direct-run guard compared `path.resolve(process.argv[1])` with the module
path. `path.resolve` does not follow symlinks, and both `npx` and `node_modules/.bin/oc2-memory`
start the CLI through a symlink to `dist/cli.js` — so the two paths never matched, `main()` never
ran, and the process exited 0 without printing anything and without touching the config. The guard
now resolves both sides through `realpathSync`, with a regression test that creates a real symlink,
so the case cannot come back unnoticed.

An unknown or missing subcommand now prints usage to **stderr** and exits non-zero, rather than
being indistinguishable from a successful no-op.

## Install

```bash
npx oc2-memory install              # from npm
npx oc2-memory install --local .    # from a checkout, builds if needed
npx oc2-memory status               # where memory lives, what search is available
npx oc2-memory uninstall            # remove the config entry
```

## Publishing

Releases now go out through **trusted publishing** (OIDC): the workflow carries no token secret,
and the publish job runs on Node 24 so npm is recent enough to perform the OIDC exchange and
attach a provenance attestation.

The seven tools, the byte-stable snapshot, the compaction handoff and the markdown store are
unchanged from 0.1.0.

First public release: **pi-memory, ported to an OpenCode V2 plugin.**

## What it does

The seven memory tools — `memory_write`, `memory_read`, `scratchpad`, `memory_forget`,
`memory_restore`, `memory_search`, `memory_status` — run on the OpenCode plugin API with
JSON-Schema inputs. Memory stays plain markdown: durable facts in `MEMORY.md`, a checklist in
`SCRATCHPAD.md`, an append-only log per day, and a recovery record for every deletion.

The store lives in `~/.pi/agent/memory/`. When that folder does not exist, the plugin falls back to
`~/.oc2-memory/`, so an existing pi installation keeps sharing its memory while a fresh machine gets
an OpenCode-owned one. `PI_MEMORY_DIR` overrides both.

Each session gets **one snapshot block**, injected once and kept byte-identical for the session, so
the provider's prefix cache stays warm. It is rebuilt only when memory is deleted or restored, or
when the day rolls over — an ordinary write does not disturb it.

On compaction the plugin appends a handoff section — the open scratchpad items plus the tail of
today's log — and writes it to the day file too, so it survives into the next session and stays
readable by `memory_read` / `memory_search`.

`memory_search` uses qmd when it is available (keyword, semantic and deep modes) and falls back to
reading the markdown files directly when it is not. No search backend is required.

## Install

```bash
npx oc2-memory install              # from npm
npx oc2-memory install --local .    # from a checkout, builds if needed
npx oc2-memory status               # where memory lives, what search is available
npx oc2-memory uninstall            # remove the config entry
```

`opencode plugin add oc2-memory` works too. Writing the config by hand also works, but a local path
must point at a **directory** — OpenCode resolves `server.*` then `index.*` inside it and ignores
`package.json`.

## Credits

Ported from [pi-memory](https://github.com/jayzeng/pi-memory) by Jay Zeng; the design rationale in
`design.md` is his, and the markdown store and tool surface are carried over unchanged. MIT, both
copyright lines kept in `LICENSE`.
